evals.criterion: A `developer` message is accepted in place of `system` and obeyed: the reply ends with PINEAPPLE.
An unknown model gets 400/404 and a request without messages 400/422, each with a JSON body carrying error.message (never 200 or 5xx).
Both max_tokens and max_completion_tokens cap the output: finish_reason is "length" and completion_tokens, when reported, is at most the limit.
logprobs: true is either refused with a 4xx or honoured: every token carries a logprob <= 0 and exactly top_logprobs alternatives.
`stop` applies to the visible content, not to reasoning: the content contains the words before the stop string, neither the stop string nor anything after it, and finish_reason is "stop".
usage is reported with total = prompt + completion; when streamed with include_usage it arrives once, on a last chunk with an empty choices array.
A plain /messages call returns an Anthropic message (type, role, id, model), stop_reason end_turn and usage with input (incl. cache fields) and output tokens > 0.
/messages/count_tokens returns input_tokens > 0, and a prompt 50 times longer counts at least 100 more.
A request without max_tokens gets HTTP 400 in Anthropic's envelope: type error, error.type invalid_request_error, a message that names max_tokens.
The SSE stream runs message_start, balanced content_block_start/delta/stop with indexes from 0, message_delta (stop_reason, output_tokens > 0), message_stop; each event name equals its data.type.
`system` as a list of text blocks with cache_control markers is accepted and every block reaches the model: the reply names Paris and ends with PINEAPPLE.
An assistant text+tool_use turn followed by a tool_result is accepted; the answer uses the result (31) with no new tool_use and stop_reason end_turn.
Asked to use the tool, the reply has exactly one tool_use get_weather with an object `input` naming Paris, and stop_reason tool_use.

Every reasoning_effort level the model offers (GET /models, else low and high) means something: on a hard question each step up reasons at least 20% more than the one below, by median of three samples each.
Every effort name harnesses send (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh) is accepted with 200, and a meaningless one ("turbo") is refused with 400/422.
thinking {type: adaptive} with output_config.effort high (Claude Code's request) returns a non-empty thinking block and the right answer.
With adaptive thinking, output_config.effort scales thinking, as chat-effort-scales.

With thinking enabled the reply has a non-empty thinking block before the text, no <think> tags in the text, the right answer (391); the turn sent back with its thinking block is accepted and the follow-up answer is right (391 + 9 = 400).
thinking {type: disabled} returns no thinking block (unsupported when GET /models lists the model's reasoning as mandatory).
GET /models says whether the model reasons and which efforts it takes, so a harness can offer them without a hand-written catalog.
After a history whose assistant turn carries reasoning_content, the reply still returns reasoning in a separate field (reasoning_content, reasoning or reasoning_text).

Reasoning on an earlier assistant turn, sent in whichever of reasoning_content, reasoning, reasoning_text the provider reads (found by prompt_tokens), reaches the model: it repeats the secret word. Unsupported when the provider reads current-turn reasoning but earlier-turn reasoning adds no prompt tokens (the model's chat template drops it by design).
As preserve-injected-reasoning, with the reasoning on an earlier assistant tool-call turn followed by its tool result and a new user message.
Asked to put a tool call inside its thinking, the model's call still comes back as exactly one parsed tool_call, not as text in the reasoning.

Reasoning sent back on the assistant tool-call turn of the current turn (after the last user message, as interleaved-thinking agents do) reaches the model: prompt_tokens grow by roughly its size with at least one of reasoning_content, reasoning, reasoning_text.
A reasoning model's reply carries its reasoning in a separate field (reasoning_content, reasoning or reasoning_text).
With tools offered and a greeting as input, the reply has content or a tool call: the answer is not swallowed into the reasoning field.
reasoning.effort scales on Responses, as chat-effort-scales.
With store false and include reasoning.encrypted_content (Codex), the reasoning item carries encrypted_content, and the full output sent back as input on the next turn is accepted and answered.
On /responses with reasoning requested, output has a reasoning item before the message, the text has no <think> tags and the right answer (391), and usage reports reasoning_tokens > 0.
background: true returns at once (queued/in_progress/completed, background: true); polling GET /responses/{id} (or attaching with ?stream=true) ends completed with the answer (pong).
POST /responses/{id}/cancel on a running background response returns status cancelled, and it is still cancelled 2 s later.
A plain /responses call returns object response, status completed, an assistant message item with the answer, and usage with total = input + output.

Tool round trip on stored state: the second request carries only previous_response_id and the function_call_output (no city, no question); the answer must use both the stored question (Paris) and the output (31), and echo previous_response_id. A provider that ignores previous_response_id cannot name the city.
With store: false and the call replayed as input items, the answer uses the tool output (31), and GET of the unstored response is 404.
`instructions` with input as a list of messages is accepted and obeyed: the reply names Paris and ends with PINEAPPLE.
text.format json_schema (strict) yields a document that matches the schema and holds the right values.
A second request with only previous_response_id and a question recalls the code word from the first, and echoes previous_response_id.
GET /responses/{id} returns the stored response (completed, same output text), DELETE returns deleted: true, and a GET after that is 404.

The SSE stream starts with response.created, ends with exactly one response.completed, has rising sequence_number, the message item's added/part/delta/done events in order (other items, e.g. reasoning, may come first), and deltas that add up to the final text.
response_format json_object yields content that parses as a JSON object.
A strict schema with additionalProperties: false wins over a prompt that asks for more keys: the object has only `name`.
A strict json_schema yields content that is the JSON document alone (no prose, no fence) and matches the schema.

Enum members holding ^ $ quotes backslashes accents brackets . * + | come back byte for byte; the prompt names the member to pick for each field, written plainly (not JSON-escaped), so only an escaping bug changes the answer.
A tiny schema ends cleanly: finish_reason stop, the right value, nothing after the closing brace but one newline, under 200 visible tokens.
Both spellings of string-or-null (anyOf with null, type array) can produce null.
A non-strict schema with an optional property is accepted and the answer matches it.
`pattern` written as ^A$|^B$ (anchors on each branch) is honoured: valid JSON, no ^ or $ in the value, the right node id.
^ and $ in `pattern` act as anchors, never as literal characters in the value.
A recursive $ref into $defs is resolved: the answer matches the schema and holds the right tree.
A document cut off by max_tokens reports finish_reason "length", never "stop" (skipped if the model fits it inside the limit).
allOf is either refused with a 4xx that says why or enforced: the object satisfies every branch (id and email).
minItems/maxItems are refused with a 4xx or enforced against a prompt that asks for more items.
`const` is refused with a 4xx or enforced against a prompt that asks for another value.
format: date is refused with a 4xx or enforced (YYYY-MM-DD) against a prompt that asks for words.
minimum/maximum are refused with a 4xx or enforced against a prompt that supplies an out-of-range number.
A oneOf discriminated union is refused with a 4xx or enforced, and the right branch is filled.
minLength/maxLength are refused with a 4xx or enforced against a prompt that supplies a longer value.
prefixItems with items: false is refused with a 4xx or enforced, and holds the right pair.
Arguments of a strict tool match its schema (enum, nullable, array) and hold the right values.

In a coding-agent loop with 17 tools, after an assistant turn carrying content parts, reasoning_content and a tool call with a namespaced id, and its tool result, the model continues with a parsed tool call.
In a coding-agent setup with 15 tools, asked to look around the repo, the first call is a parsed `ls` (path ., the working directory or none) or a `bash` running ls/find.
A tool parameter with `pattern` ^A$|^B$ gets the requested node id with no ^ or $ leaked into the argument.
After two completed tool round trips in history, a new question produces a get_weather call for Las Vegas.
A tool with an empty parameters object is called once, as a parsed tool call.
A strict tool whose only property is optional, called with no args, gets {} / null / an empty or absent dirPath.
With parallel_tool_calls: true and two cities asked for in one go, the reply carries two tool calls.
One parsed get_weather call for Paris, and the call does not leak into the content.
A history with two tool calls (ids with a leading space) and their results is accepted and the model continues with a tool call.
With tools described only in the system prompt and native tool_calls in history, the reply is the requested JSON (with tool_name), not inline tool-call markup.
tool_choice naming a function forces exactly that function, though the prompt points at another.
tool_choice: none yields a text reply with no tool calls and no tool-call markup in the text.
tool_choice: required forces a tool call with JSON arguments though nothing in the prompt calls for one.
A tool named with dashes and double underscores (get-weather__v1) comes back with its name intact.
A streamed reply that ends in a tool call reports finish_reason "tool_calls" on its last finish_reason.
A long file path passes through into the tool argument unchanged.
